newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia sees Gabcikovo suit end in October.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia sees Gabcikovo suit end in October.

text.p: Slovakia expects the International Court of Justice in the Hague to come to a final ruling on a Hungarian law suit over the controversial Gabcikovo dam project this autumn, a senior official said on Wednesday.

The two neighbours are locked in a dispute over Slovakia's unilateral decision to divert a considerable amount of water from the Danube River for the project in 1992, after Hungary quit a joint agreement which planned a similar dam on its side.
"Taking experience with the court into account, we expect its ruling in September or October this year," Peter Tomka, Slovakia's representative at the Hague's court told a news conference.
However, Tomka said there was still room for an out-of-court settlement. The two sides opened talks on an expert level exploring a settlement at the same time they asked the court for ruling.
"It is possible to reach a settlement at any moment right up until the court's final ruling is announced," Tomka said declining to elaborate.
Both countries officially presented their cases at the International Court in the Hague in 1993, which then announced it would begin holding public hearings on March 3.

Slovakia claims Hungary was the first to breach a contract, originally signed in 1977 by communist leaders of both countries, while the Hungarian side says a diversion of the Danube flow breaks international law.
